claims.claim: An EPC is legally required when a property is sold or let.
claims.quote: You must have an EPC when you’re: selling a property renting out a property building a new property
claims.note: The source states the general requirement but also lists buildings and circumstances that do not need an EPC.

claims.claim: Buyers can search for an EPC for free.
claims.quote: Use the find an energy certificate service to check if your property has a valid EPC and download it for free.
claims.note: The service allows a free EPC check and download.

claims.claim: Landlords renting property in England and Wales must have an EPC rating of E or above.
claims.quote: Since 1 April 2020, landlords can no longer let or continue to let properties covered by the MEES Regulations if they have an EPC rating below E, unless they have a valid exemption in place.
claims.note: The E minimum applies to covered domestic private rented properties and allows valid exemptions, not every rental property.
